label: Classic — High key
brief: High key (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High-key_lighting): a bright, light-toned image with few deep shadows and gentle contrast. Most tones sit above middle grey; whites come close to white but keep texture in skin, fabric and cloud. Raise exposure and shadows, lower contrast, and lift the blacks a little rather than crushing them; keep the highlights from clipping (the clipping limits still hold). Keep colour clean and light: lower saturation slightly if bright colours turn loud. If the scene is dark by nature (night, a dark interior, a black subject), say so and suggest another look instead of forcing it.
convergence_hints: stop when the photo reads light and airy and the brightest areas still hold texture
stop when no deep shadow pulls the eye

checks.why: high key: the median tone sits above middle grey, in Zone VI or higher
high key: few deep shadows, Zones 0-II under 5% of the frame
